answer: A single thread of proof-of-personhood links new agents to existing ones, so forging thousands of identities requires bonding every fake key. Sybil resistance via staked identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, mapped on a public atlas of verified keys. Under a gale of cheap registrations, attackers face rising capital costs and slashing risk, making mass identity creation economically irrational while honest agents recover their stake.
